description: Local network (LAN) model sharing, incorporated into this build per explicit user request. This was NEVER previously implemented (the spec Section 9.3 only constrained local calls to loopback; no peer/LAN/mDNS feature exists and no branch implemented one). Scope it sensibly to stay shippable under INTEGRATIONS_ONLY (no live cross-machine network to test): (A) CONSUME a peer's models - let the user add a LAN peer as a general host:port OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g. another machine's Ollama/LM Studio/Agent Harbor) so its models enumerate and route like any provider; this reuses the existing ProviderConfig + base-url posture (check_provider_base_url already ACCEPTS non-loopback with a plaintext->TLS warning and blocks only link-local/metadata IPs), and is fully unit-testable with wiremock. (B) SHARE/serve - a toggle that runs a small local HTTP endpoint re-exposing THIS instance's local models (Ollama/LM Studio/embedded) to peers, behind a clean seam; live cross-machine verification is user-only. (C) DISCOVERY - peer discovery (mDNS/UDP broadcast) behind a trait with a manual-entry fallback; live discovery is user-only. Land A solidly + testably; scaffold B and C cleanly with visible non-fatal behavior and clear user-only flags. This is a DIFFERENT feature from the embedded folder-scan model-library rework (which stays out of scope).
steps: Decide and document the concrete model in findings before coding: (A) a LAN peer is represented as a ProviderConfig row of an OpenAI-compatible kind (reuse ProviderKind::GenericOpenAI, or add a dedicated peer marker in `extra`) with a REQUIRED host:port base_url (e.g. http://192.168.1.50:11434/v1) and an optional label; it is treated as a local-network provider (NOT loopback-local for the privacy hard-constraint: a LAN peer is off-host, so it must NOT satisfy a LocalOnly/Confidential tag - confirm local_provider_ids only includes provable on-host locality, so LAN peers are correctly excluded from the LocalOnly gate). Record this privacy decision explicitly.

Backend CONSUME commands (crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs, each with `_inner`, mirroring set_local_runtime/set_cloud_provider): `add_network_peer(baseUrl, label?, apiKey?) -> NetworkPeerView` (validate baseUrl via check_provider_base_url - a Blocked link-local/metadata target rejects; a non-loopback plaintext target returns the existing TLS warning; persist a ProviderConfig with a stable per-peer id derived from the base_url/label; store an optional key as a SecretRef), `list_network_peers() -> Vec<NetworkPeerView>` (display-safe: id/label/baseUrl/hasApiKey, never the key), `remove_network_peer(id) -> ()` (delete secret if any + row). Emit CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged on add/remove success so peer models enumerate immediately. Register all three in lib.rs generate_handler!. _inner unit tests with InMemorySecretStore + in-memory Db: add persists + shows in list + hasApiKey; blocked base_url rejects; non-loopback plaintext yields a warning; remove deletes secret + row.

Confirm peer models flow through the EXISTING enumeration + routing with no pipeline change: because a peer is a normal ProviderConfig of an OpenAI-compatible kind, list_available_models_inner and the send_message registry build already pick it up. Add a providers-crate/wiremock test proving an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at an arbitrary (mock) base_url enumerates models via the shared native adapter (this is the offline proof for the consume path).

Backend SHARE/serve seam (scaffold cleanly, live use is user-only): add a small module (prefer a host-verifiable crate, e.g. a new crates/net-share or a module in orchestrator-core/providers) defining a `ModelShareServer` trait/struct that, when started, serves an OpenAI-compatible read surface (at minimum GET /v1/models, and optionally proxying /v1/chat/completions to the local provider) bound to the LAN interface on a configurable port. Add commands `set_model_sharing(enabled: bool, port?) -> ModelSharingView` and `get_model_sharing() -> ModelSharingView` persisting an ADDITIVE AppConfig.model_sharing { enabled, port } (#[serde(default)], forward-compatible). Starting/stopping the server is wired but must degrade to a VISIBLE non-fatal status if the port is unavailable (never a silent hang). Register the commands. Unit-test the request handler logic (models listing serialization) offline; flag that binding to a real LAN interface + peer reachability is user-only. Document the security posture: sharing binds to the LAN and re-exposes local models, so it is OFF by default and the UI states it exposes models to the local network.

Backend DISCOVERY seam (scaffold, live use user-only): define a `PeerDiscovery` trait with `discover(timeout) -> Vec<DiscoveredPeer { label, baseUrl }>` and a default implementation stub (mDNS/UDP broadcast) that, in-sandbox, returns an empty list without error. Add a command `discover_network_peers() -> Vec<DiscoveredPeerView>` that runs discovery with a bounded timeout and returns display-safe results; on any error returns an empty list + the frontend shows a non-fatal 'no peers found / discovery unavailable' notice. Register it. Unit-test the result mapping offline; flag live discovery as user-only.

IPC + types: add wrappers (addNetworkPeer, listNetworkPeers, removeNetworkPeer, setModelSharing, getModelSharing, discoverNetworkPeers) in frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts and camelCase TS types in frontend/src/types/index.ts (NetworkPeerView, ModelSharingView, DiscoveredPeerView, and any enums). Keep the hand-mirror exact.

Frontend Settings 'Network Sharing' section: create frontend/src/features/settings/NetworkSharingSection.tsx and register it in Settings.tsx SECTIONS (id 'networkSharing', label 'Network Sharing'). It (1) lists configured LAN peers with Add (baseUrl + optional label + optional key) and Remove, rehydrating from list_network_peers on mount and surfacing the base-url warning; (2) offers a 'Discover peers' button (discover_network_peers) that lists found peers with a one-click Add, showing a non-fatal 'no peers found' notice when empty; (3) has a 'Share my local models on the network' toggle (set_model_sharing) with an optional port, showing the current status from get_model_sharing and a clear security note that this exposes local models to the LAN (OFF by default). Every input gets an explicit aria-label. Added peers appear under Local-network in the model picker (they enumerate via the existing providers store load()).

Confirm the peer models show in the composer's inline model control (from FEAT-002): since they are ProviderConfig rows, they enumerate through list_available_models; ensure the picker groups them clearly (e.g. a 'Network' group distinct from on-host Local and Cloud) so the user can tell a LAN peer apart. This is a small presentation addition to the inline model control / ProviderModelPicker grouping.
CSS: reuse settings-form styles; add any minimal peer-list / network-group styles via var(--ah-*).

Tests: Rust _inner + wiremock tests as above (add/list/remove peer; blocked vs warning base_url; OpenAI-compatible enumeration at a mock base_url; model-sharing handler serialization; discovery result mapping). Frontend vitest: NetworkSharingSection add/list/remove peer (mock invoke), discover shows peers or non-fatal empty notice, sharing toggle reflects status; the model picker shows a Network group when a peer is configured. Add ALL new commands to every mounting test's routeInvoke (settings.test.tsx, app.test.tsx) with well-formed shapes and initialize any new store fields in resets; use await findBy*/waitFor.
acceptance_criteria: A user can add a LAN peer by host:port (OpenAI-compatible) whose models then enumerate and route exactly like any provider; the base-url posture rejects link-local/metadata targets and warns on non-loopback plaintext.
A LAN peer is treated as OFF-host: it does NOT satisfy a LocalOnly/Confidential privacy tag (local_provider_ids only includes provable on-host locality); this decision is documented.

Consume path is proven offline: a wiremock/host-verifiable test shows an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at an arbitrary base_url enumerating models via the shared native adapter, plus _inner tests for add/list/remove peer.

A 'Share my local models on the network' toggle + a small ModelShareServer seam exist (OFF by default, visible non-fatal status on port failure, security note in the UI); its request-handler logic is unit-tested offline; live LAN binding/reachability is flagged user-only.
A peer-discovery seam + discover_network_peers command exist with a manual-entry fallback and a non-fatal empty/unavailable notice; live discovery is flagged user-only.

New commands (add_network_peer, list_network_peers, remove_network_peer, set_model_sharing, get_model_sharing, discover_network_peers) are registered in generate_handler!, have IPC wrappers + camelCase TS types, and pass their _inner/unit tests.
A Settings 'Network Sharing' section manages peers, discovery, and the share toggle; the model picker distinguishes Network peers from on-host Local and Cloud.
Frontend vitest + Rust tests pass; tsc/eslint/prettier clean (or CI-only with exhaustive manual review). No regression to loopback-local privacy semantics, enumeration, or send.
verification: Run `cargo test -p providers` (and the crate hosting the share/discovery seams) for the wiremock enumeration + handler + discovery-mapping tests - runnable in-sandbox if those crates build offline; otherwise CI-only with manual review.

cargo test for the command _inner tests is CI-only (tauri-app needs crates.io) - manual self-review of command bodies, registration, IPC/type parity, secret handling, and the privacy (off-host) decision.
Frontend vitest for NetworkSharingSection + model-picker Network grouping; confirm the non-fatal discovery/sharing fallbacks. CI-only if node_modules absent, with manual review of mocks.
Confirm the privacy gate: add a routing/pipeline-level assertion or manual trace that a LAN peer is excluded from local_provider_ids so a LocalOnly/Confidential conversation never routes to a peer.
